Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time shut down, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, which focuses on richer social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media previously announced that it would be closing down the TV tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as a 'watchlist with speed, beauty, and fun community features'.

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms. For users still looking for a TV Time alternative, this app can be considered the 'spiritual successor' of the defunct platform—TV Time was once one of the most widely used TV tracking apps in the world.

Former TV Time users who backed up their data via the export tool before the platform shut down can import their archives into Bingers, seamlessly continuing their existing records; users who never exported their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app before, can start building their watchlist from scratch.

Bingers places strong emphasis on community-driven features, including personal profiles, comments, show ratings, GIF stickers, polls, and character popularity votes. Pinto told TechCrunch that these are exactly the features that made TV Time so popular over the years:

If users simply want to keep track of the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Like TV Time, the platform also displays a calendar of upcoming and premiere episodes, along with a countdown showing how many days until airing.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store and currently has no in-app purchases.
